newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse session slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse session slightly higher.

text.p: German equities ended floor trade on Thursday marginally higher, with a mixed performance across the DAX index of German shares ahead of U.S. jobless claims data due later in the day.
The DAX 30-share index ended the session 3.52 points, or 0.14 percent higher, at 2,570.32 on small turnover.
"It looks as if we're going nowhere at the moment until the U.S. numbers," said one trader.
The dollar firmed to about 1.5130 marks and helped underpin trade during the session.
The U.S. data will be closely examined for clues on the timing and extent of future U.S. interest rate moves.
U.S. producer prices are expected to rise between 0.1 and 0.2 percent in August, with U.S. jobless claims in the latest 7-month period expected to gain between 315,000 and 360,000.
Any indications of inflationary pressures in the U.S. could hit German shares hard, dealer said.

Germany's Deutsche Bank AG ended the day up 35 pfennigs at 71.60 marks after news of an upgrade from "hold" to "buy" from investment bank UBS provided relief from recent problems with its British asset management unit.

Carmaker BMW ended down 50 pfennigs at 867.50 marks, having earlier lost 8.00 marks to 860 after a company forecast that full-year earnings growth would be around the 10 percent level of the first half.
The news was seen as disappointing more bullish market expectations.
